source_authorization: User/planner explicitly authorized one bounded Pilot16 refinement after reviewing the completed 16-image pilot diagnostics.
scientific_question: Can more conservative NP early-population pruning retain the current EPP rescue mechanism while reducing catastrophic harms, at the same dominant NP compute as four independent NP-1 trajectories?

compute_policy.within_np_family_primary_proxy: UNet forward evaluations at identical model, resolution, scheduler, and measurement operator
compute_policy.wall_time_role: engineering diagnostic only; not the scientific matching variable
compute_policy.cross_family_policy: Do not equate one NP UNet evaluation with one DAPS or SITCOM unit. Before final cross-family claims, report/calibrate method-specific FLOPs or a defensible forward/operator-equivalent compute accounting and compare at fixed or similar compute.
compute_policy.headline_requirement: A refined NP method is useful only if it improves recovery relative to established baselines/controls at fixed or similar compute; internal EPP-vs-EPP gains alone are not the final scientific endpoint.

NP_EPP_321_NO_REALLOCATION.note: Intentionally lower compute. Report its actual Work-FRE; do not present it as compute matched.

execution_scope.measurements: Reuse exactly the already-materialized frozen Pilot16 development measurements; generate no new measurement.

decision_context.pilot_failure_motivation: Current EPP can rescue a bad basin (e.g. D/30740) but can catastrophically lose a good independent root under 4->2 pruning (e.g. D/11775).
decision_context.bounded_change: Only the survival schedule and corresponding fixed-budget proposal allocation change: 4->3->2->1 at the same checkpoints 72/148/300. The measurement score, parent NP dynamics, total matched work, and terminal selector remain frozen.

resource_contract.reason_no_new_memory_calibration: EPP321 processes branches sequentially; its largest per-branch candidate count is 9, below the already-calibrated current EPP maximum of 20, while live branch state storage is small relative to candidate activations.
